items.title: Align Bazel release builds with Cargo and fix platform compatibility
items.body:
Align Bazel release builds with Cargo and fix platform compatibility

## Why

Bazel release builds need Cargo-compatible Rust and native build-script settings. Platform-specific issues also include Windows command-line limits, MSVC runtime conflicts with V8's allocator, and a missing V8 `__clear_cache` symbol on ARM64 musl.

## What changed

- Add `--config=release` settings for thin LTO, four target codegen units, and disabled debug assertions and overflow checks, with separate settings for build tools.
- Add opt-in Cargo release profile support for build-script optimization and debug information, preserving explicit C/C++ flags. Give optimized Bubblewrap builds `-O3`, debug symbols, and enabled native assertions.
- Statically link the MSVC CRT for Rust and C/C++ target and host dependencies, and disable SQLite intrinsics on x64 MSVC to avoid startup crashes on older CPUs.
- Let the Rust process wrapper read its arguments from a multiline parameter file to avoid Windows command-line limits.
- Select the ARM64 musl V8 archive containing compiler-rt builtins and raise the Rust recursion limit to `256` in the app-server client, exec, and TUI entry points for release compilation.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)? 26.1002.52244 ### What subscription do you have? Pro ### What platform is your computer? Office PC: Windows 11 Pro, version 23H2, OS build 22631.6199 ### What issue are you seeing?

Summary

ChatGPT Work / Codex Desktop on Windows cannot connect to local SQL Server Express using Windows Integrated Authentication from within its sandbox.

The issue has been reproduced on two Windows computers with different sandbox configurations. SQL Server and Windows Authentication work correctly outside Work on both machines.

The two environments exhibit different failures.

Office PC — SSPI credential acquisition failure

  • Windows 11 Pro 23H2, build 22631.6199

  • Desktop version: 26.1002.52244

  • Sandbox: unelevated

  • Windows identity and AuthenticationId match normal PowerShell.

  • Work token: IsTokenRestricted=True.

  • Normal PowerShell token: IsTokenRestricted=False.

Calling AcquireCredentialsHandleW with default credentials and SECPKG_CRED_OUTBOUND produces:

SSPI package | Normal PowerShell | Work -- | -- | -- Negotiate | 0x00000000 | 0x8009030E NTLM | 0x00000000 | 0x8009030E

SQL connection errors include:

  • Microsoft.Data.SqlClient: "The target principal name is incorrect. Cannot generate SSPI context."

  • sqlcmd: 0x8009030E — No credentials are available in the security package.

  • Invoke-Sqlcmd: "Failed to generate SSPI context."

The failure occurs during SSPI credential acquisition, before connecting to SQL Server.

An earlier sandbox setup failure also reported helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors, with Windows error 32 while attempting to update permissions on a locked node_repl.exe file. Its relationship to the SSPI failure is unknown.

Home PC — SQL shared-memory access denied

  • Desktop version: 26.930.31730, build 12947

  • Sandbox: elevated

  • Work process: AppContainer, low integrity, not running as administrator

  • IsTokenRestricted=False

  • SSPI Negotiate and NTLM both succeed inside and outside Work.

An explicit SQL shared-memory connection using lpc: succeeds from normal PowerShell but fails from Work:

  • Shared Memory Provider, error 40

  • SQL error number 5

  • Inner Win32 error 5: "Access is denied."

The failure occurs before any SQL query executes.

Expected resolution

Please investigate whether these behaviors are expected sandbox limitations or defects.

I need an officially supported solution that preserves sandbox isolation and Windows Integrated Authentication under the current Windows user.

I do not want to disable the sandbox, run the agent with administrator privileges, modify SQL authentication, or introduce alternative SQL credentials.

Feedback references

Office PC:
0515b81c-8b5d-4043-802a-dd95adbef03f

Home PC:
no-active-thread-01a1185a-f9ef-7223-bdc0-7410353c3f91

No system, SQL Server, sandbox, permission, repository, or database configuration was changed during diagnostics.

### What steps can reproduce the bug? ## Prerequisites - Windows computer with ChatGPT Work / Codex Desktop installed. - Local SQL Server Express instance. - Windows user with permission to connect using Windows Integrated Authentication. - Codex Windows sandbox enabled. - PowerShell running normally (non-elevated) for comparison. ## Reproduction A — Office PC (`unelevated` sandbox) 1. Configure Codex with `[windows] sandbox = "unelevated"`. 2. Open normal, non-elevated PowerShell. 3. Execute `whoami /all` and confirm the Windows identity. 4. Open a Codex Work session and execute the same command. 5. Compare the security tokens, including `AuthenticationId` and `IsTokenRestricted`. 6. In both environments, call the Windows API `AcquireCredentialsHandleW` using: - SSPI packages: `Negotiate` and `NTLM`. - Default Windows credentials. - `SECPKG_CRED_OUTBOUND`. - Null principal and null authentication data. 7. Compare the return codes. 8. Attempt a SQL Server connection using Windows Integrated Authentication from Work. **Observed result:** - Both processes use the same Windows identity and AuthenticationId. - Normal PowerShell: `IsTokenRestricted=False`. - Work: `IsTokenRestricted=True`. - Both SSPI packages succeed outside Work (`0x00000000`). - Both fail inside Work (`0x8009030E`). - SQL connections fail with SSPI context errors. ## Reproduction B — Home PC (`elevated` sandbox) 1. Use Codex Desktop with `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"`. 2. Confirm that the Work process runs inside an AppContainer with low integrity and `TokenElevation=0`. 3. Verify that SQL Server Express accepts Windows Authentication from normal, non-elevated PowerShell. 4. Verify that `AcquireCredentialsHandleW` succeeds for Negotiate and NTLM both inside and outside Work. 5. From normal PowerShell, connect to SQL Server using explicit shared memory: `Data Source=lpc:DESKTOP-RC44UPG\SQLEXPRESS;Initial Catalog=master;Integrated Security=True;Connect Timeout=5;Application Name=Work ReadOnly Authentication Diagnostic` 6. Execute a read-only diagnostic query: `SELECT SYSTEM_USER AS LoginName, ORIGINAL_LOGIN() AS OriginalLogin, DB_NAME() AS DatabaseName;` 7. Repeat the identical connection and query from a PowerShell process launched by Work. **Observed result:** - Normal PowerShell connects successfully using Windows Authentication and shared memory. - Work obtains default SSPI credentials successfully. - Work cannot open the SQL shared-memory connection. - SQL Server reports Shared Memory Provider error 40. - The exception chain contains Win32 error 5: `Access is denied`. - No SELECT executes inside Work. ## Additional notes - SQL Server Management Studio successfully connects using Windows Authentication outside Work on both computers. - No administrative privileges are required for the diagnostic commands. - No configuration changes, permission modifications, SQL writes, or sandbox bypasses were performed. - The failures were observed on October 7, 2026. - The reproduction may depend on the exact Desktop version, Windows security token, sandbox implementation, and SQL Server local transport configuration. ## Related feedback IDs Office: `0515b81c-8b5d-4043-802a-dd95adbef03f` Home: `no-active-thread-01a1185a-f9ef-7223-bdc0-7410353c3f91` ### What is the expected behavior? ChatGPT Work / Codex Desktop should be able to access a local SQL Server instance using Windows Integrated Authentication under the current Windows user's identity while keeping the Windows sandbox enabled. Expected behavior: - Default SSPI credential acquisition (Negotiate and NTLM) succeeds when the user has valid Windows credentials. - The sandbox permits supported, authorized local SQL Server connections without disabling isolation. - SQL Server connections using Integrated Security=True succeed when the same Windows user has the necessary permissions. - Read-only SQL queries execute successfully against authorized databases. - The behavior remains consistent after restarting Codex Desktop. If direct SQL Server shared-memory access is intentionally unsupported inside AppContainer, please document this limitation and provide an officially supported alternative that preserves sandbox isolation and Windows Authentication. The solution must not require disabling the sandbox, running the agent as administrator, changing SQL Server authentication, or introducing separate SQL credentials. ### Additional information This issue is blocking an active .NET 10 / Windows Forms ERP development workflow that previously worked correctly with Windows Integrated Authentication. The application repository and SQL Server databases remain functional outside Codex Desktop. Two diagnostic feedback reports have already been submitted: - Office PC: `0515b81c-8b5d-4043-802a-dd95adbef03f` - Home PC: `no-active-thread-01a1185a-f9ef-7223-bdc0-7410353c3f91` The two computers use different Desktop versions and sandbox configurations, and the observed failure mechanisms differ. A common root cause has not been established. The office PC also previously experienced a sandbox setup error involving a locked `node_repl.exe` file (Win32 error 32). Its relationship to the authentication issue is unknown. Please advise whether these behaviors are expected sandbox limitations or known defects, and identify any officially supported remediation. Additional sanitized diagnostic logs can be provided upon request. No credentials, authentication files, or sandbox secrets will be uploaded publicly.

We do not need message contents, prompts, responses, files, or credentials.

Only minimal thread identity and selection/window metadata should be available, with explicit user permission. Minutivo would process this metadata locally.

## Expected behavior

1. The user associates chat A with project A and chat B with project B.
2. Viewing chat A in the foreground attributes active time to project A.
3. Switching to chat B updates the attribution without requiring a message.
4. Background activity in chat A does not change the selected-chat signal.
5. Multiple windows can be distinguished.
6. Missing or ambiguous selection is reported explicitly rather than returning a stale selection.

### Additional information

## Why existing signals are insufficient

- In our observed setup, the outer macOS window title only identifies ChatGPT, not the selected Codex chat.
- Loaded threads and agent runtime status do not establish which chat the user is currently viewing.
- Prompt and execution hooks do not cover read-only interaction.
- Background agents must not be counted as active user time.

We reviewed the public App Server and Hooks documentation:
- https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server
- https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks

This request concerns the official ChatGPT desktop app for macOS, specifically the Codex view, not a custom client built on codex app-server.

Is there an existing supported integration that covers this use case, or could this capability be considered for the desktop app? If this repository is not the appropriate place for this particular desktop feature, please point us to the correct tracker.

items.title: Avoid sharing violations when repairing Windows runtime ACLs
items.body:
Avoid sharing violations when repairing Windows runtime ACLs

## Why

Opening active EXE/DLL files with `MAXIMUM_ALLOWED` can request access that causes sharing violations during sandbox runtime ACL repair.

## What changed

Restrict `MAXIMUM_ALLOWED` opens to directories that need to suppress child ACL propagation. For files, request `READ_CONTROL | WRITE_DAC` only when an ACL update is needed.

Preserve the non-inheriting grant behavior from https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/49690, including existing permissions, deny ACEs, and null DACLs.

## Testing

Extend the Windows runtime repair regression test to hold `node.exe` open with `FILE_SHARE_READ` throughout repair and revalidation, while checking read/execute access and preserved denials.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1002.52244, build 13536 (verified from the installed application bundle on October 7, 2026). Affected bundled engine: codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.2.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro 20x.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0.1, build 26A434. Codex Local tasks in the desktop application.

### What issue are you seeing?

With **Follow-up behavior = Queue**, submitting a follow-up while a Local task is running takes a very long time before the queued-message **Steer** action appears and becomes usable. Previously this control appeared essentially immediately.

This is a recurring user-observed regression in **control availability before the user can press Steer**. The exact elapsed time has not yet been measured. It is not merely a report that the model takes time to act after a successful steering request.

The user expressly confirms that this occurs during ordinary active turns **without compaction**. One separate attempt to steer during compaction was accidental and is excluded as an explanation of the recurring symptom.

Impact: the intended way to correct an active task becomes unavailable for an unexplained interval. Repeatedly sending follow-ups risks adding redundant or stale instructions.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed interaction sequence; a deterministic clean-start reproduction has not been established:

1. Use a Local task in the macOS desktop app with Queue selected for follow-ups.
2. Leave an ordinary task turn running, outside compaction.
3. Submit a short follow-up.
4. Observe the delay before the pending-message row exposes a usable Steer action.
5. Measure queue-row appearance, Steer visibility, dispatch acceptance, and model consumption separately.

The symptom was reported across ongoing tasks. No controlled single-window versus multiple-window comparison has yet been completed locally.

### What is the expected behavior?

A queued follow-up should receive prompt visible acknowledgement. When steering is eligible, its control should become available promptly. If steering is temporarily unavailable, show its actual state and reason rather than leaving the user waiting without an explanation.

### Additional information

**Verified text-only feedback receipt:** `no-active-thread-01a11810-9248-7b62-93c8-16cf8f97a488`.

Feedback was submitted through the supported `feedback/upload` App Server API using standalone CLI 0.161.0. That submission transport is separate from the affected desktop's bundled 0.162.0-alpha.2 engine. Logs, trace files, screenshots, attachments and source-thread association were excluded.

Sanitized local diagnostic summary, not raw diagnostic data:

- Two local performance captures showed maximum input latency of approximately 3.21 seconds and 0.60 seconds respectively. Profiling startup overhead was considered separately.
- A Queue request in the second capture was accepted in 128 ms. This does **not** measure the time until Steer was painted or usable.
- A bounded 40-minute log review counted 308 `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` records in the primary renderer. These are log records, not 308 distinct user failures.
- The same review found zero `Queued follow-up changed before dispatch` and zero send-lock release failures.
- The renderer warnings, window ownership, and concurrent stream reconnects have **not** been proved causal.

Related reports were reviewed before filing:

- #51251 concerns clicking an already available Steer control / shortcut and dispatch failure. This report concerns the preceding delay in making that control available.
- #49456 concerns already accepted input remaining pending and stale owner snapshots. Its multi-window comment is a useful lead, but that sequence is not established locally.
- #50702 describes Windows controls remaining absent after an update and loss of a recovery path; this report describes macOS control-appearance latency.
- #51610 and #43228 concern delayed consumption after steering; that is a separate timing boundary.

Please investigate queue admission, pending-row rendering, and Steer eligibility/visibility during normal active Local turns. If these symptoms share an existing root cause, please link the appropriate tracking issue. No specific cause, permanent message loss, or successful workaround is asserted.

Private task content, identifiers, legal material, account data and filesystem paths are omitted.

items.body:
# Windows desktop repeatedly hangs with stale `CODEX_CLI_PATH` override

## Summary

The Codex Windows desktop app repeatedly becomes permanently unresponsive. The composer often shows an attachment chip with an endless loading spinner. Killing `ChatGPT.exe` in Task Manager restores the app, but the visible conversation does not always rehydrate even though the underlying agent/session can continue.

## Environment

- Windows 10 Pro 22H2, build 19045
- Desktop package: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1002.6548.0_x64`
- Electron/ChatGPT executable version reported by WER: `155.0.8059.27`
- User-level `CODEX_CLI_PATH` points to a persisted `.sandbox-bin/codex.exe`
- Selected app-server version: `codex-cli 0.145.0-alpha.18`, dated 2026-07-18
- The current package contains a different `resources/codex.exe`

## Evidence

- Windows Event Viewer recorded 341 `Application Hang` / `MoAppHang` events for Codex over 60 days, all reported as `Top level window is idle`.
- Seventeen hangs occurred on package `26.1002.6548.0` on 2026-10-07.
- Startup logs explicitly report the app-server executable as the user override and `source=override`.
- The desktop repeatedly sends `app/installed`; the selected old app-server rejects it with JSON-RPC error `-32600`, `Invalid request: unknown variant app/installed`.
- There were 11,344 such rejections in one day. Pending request counts reached more than 1,000 in some sessions.
- Terminated sessions commonly end with `write EPIPE` from the IPC router.
- Binary inspection confirms that the overridden old binary contains `plugin/installed` but not `app/installed`; the current packaged binary contains `app/installed`.
- Session transcripts remain present and continue to update after the window is killed. On restart, logs show durable WebSocket reconnection and thread-resume activity, explaining why work can continue while the UI loses the displayed chat.
- The system drive was also critically low on space (approximately 151 MB free), which likely compounds profile/database and update failures, but the protocol mismatch is independently reproducible in the logs.

## Expected behavior

The desktop app should either ignore an incompatible `CODEX_CLI_PATH`, perform a compatibility check before using it, or present a clear blocking error. A rejected background request should not accumulate indefinitely or freeze the renderer.

## Suggested safeguards

1. Validate the overridden app-server protocol/version during initialization.
2. Fall back to the packaged binary when required methods are missing.
3. Add backoff/deduplication for repeatedly rejected `app/installed` requests.
4. Preserve and rehydrate the current conversation after renderer or top-level-window failure.
5. Surface low-disk-space warnings before Chromium/SQLite state becomes unreliable.

Raw desktop logs and Windows WER report IDs are available if maintainers need them, but they are not attached publicly because they may contain conversation metadata and local paths.

labels.name: enhancement

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI/TUI, with a companion client connected to the shared app-server.

Installed version: `codex-cli 0.160.1`, macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon. The relevant completion path was also inspected in `rust-v0.161.0`; that version was not run.

### What feature would you like to see?

An opt-in way to keep unanswered `request_user_input_async` questions interactive after their originating assistant turn completes successfully, with a supported question-resolution lifecycle shared between the terminal and companion clients.

This is a feature request about an acknowledged limitation, not a new claim that the current behavior is an unintended regression. In #49146, a [maintainer explained](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49146#issuecomment-5925266552) that async controls intentionally close at turn end, and that users can subsequently answer in ordinary chat. I understand that the async tool does not block the assistant and that its acceptance receipt is not a human answer.

**Use case**

I am developing Orbit, a companion application for monitoring local agent sessions and answering questions/permissions. A user should be able to see a pending structured question in both the originating terminal and Orbit, then choose either surface to answer. The user may need longer than the remaining assistant turn to read several questions or decide.

With the current lifecycle, an unanswered question can become plain transcript text in the terminal as soon as the assistant finishes. Ordinary follow-up chat is still possible, but the original selectable choices, question navigation, and structured submission are no longer available there. Keeping a verified answer route in a companion client does not restore the terminal's controls. Thus successful turn completion can remove one of the user's intended answer surfaces even though no human decision has occurred.

**Requested behavior**

- Offer a setting or supported capability that retains pending structured questions and drafts across successful turn completion, without keeping the assistant artificially busy.
- Allow an explicit answer from the retained terminal editor or an authorized companion client while the question remains valid.
- Expose/document pending, answered, dismissed/withdrawn, and expired states sufficiently for both clients to reconcile their controls. Answers from one surface should retire the corresponding controls on the other; duplicate/conflicting submissions need defined handling.
- Handle each question independently in a multi-question request, preserving still-unanswered questions.
- Keep interruption, failure, expiry, and explicit cancellation as separate lifecycle decisions. Do not automatically submit drafts, approve tools, or replay an uncertain answer.

An opt-in approach could preserve the current default. This request is specifically about retaining **non-blocking async** question controls; it is not a request to make every async question block the assistant or to change command-approval policy.

### Additional information

**Source evidence**

In [0.160.1 `chatwidget/protocol.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.1/codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/protocol.rs#L402-L522), the live successful-completion branch calls `take_question_drafts()`. [The bottom-pane helper](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.1/codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/questions.rs#L44-L69) delegates to pending-draft recovery and documents the editor closing at turn end. The completion call remains in [0.161.0](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.161.0/codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/protocol.rs#L418-L536).

**Suggested acceptance scenario**

Emit an async question with two choices, leave it unanswered, and complete the source turn successfully. With persistence opted in, the terminal should still allow selection/submission afterward. Repeat with multiple questions and a partially typed draft. Then answer from the companion client and verify that only the corresponding terminal controls retire. Confirm that completion alone sends no answer or artificial keepalive turn.

**Evidence limits**

The loss of terminal interactivity was user-reported during Orbit development, and the source lifecycle was inspected. A clean live reproduction with Orbit disabled was not run during this investigation. Orbit also had separate connection/recovery bugs; this request does not attribute those to Codex or claim that this completion path explains every reported symptom. No private transcripts, credentials, local paths, or session identifiers are attached.

Related: #49146 (closed as intended lifecycle), #43803 (desktop final-message dismissal), #47535 (collapsed questions and combined-answer handling), and #43759 (blocking-question control, a different alternative).

Submitted at the affected user's explicit request.

items.title: Preserve diagnostic reasons for MCP user verification failures
items.body:
Preserve diagnostic reasons for MCP user verification failures

## Why

User-verification cancellations previously discarded failure reasons, leaving MCP servers unable to distinguish user cancellation from unavailable approval, interruption, or invalid proof.

## What changed

- Carry a bounded `openai/userVerificationReason` value in response `_meta` for verification failures, declines, and cancellations across the TUI, app server, and MCP client.
- Preserve recognized reasons and classify invalid responses, missing or invalid proofs, response errors, closed response channels, interruptions, and unavailable approval.
- Discard unknown reasons and unrelated metadata. Keep proof material out of decline and cancellation responses, and keep display messages and raw error diagnostics out of response metadata.

## Testing

Add and update tests for typed failure propagation, metadata filtering, invalid proofs, response-channel failures, interrupted requests, and unavailable approval, including TUI RPC and native MCP response coverage.

items.title: [ChatGPT][Regression] Existing Chat local execution is blocked and redirected to separately-metered Work

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: rate-limits
labels.description: Issues related to rate limits, quotas, and token usage reporting

labels.name: agent
labels.description: Issues related to the core agent loop

items.body:
## Summary

A previously working local-execution workflow in a normal Chat conversation has become blocked and redirected into ChatGPT Work.

On a ChatGPT Plus account, an existing long-running Project conversation had been successfully using user-authorized local execution against a Windows workspace: reading/editing local files, running commands, testing changes, and continuing the same agentic workflow in Chat.

On 2026-10-07, the same conversation could no longer perform local file/command operations directly. The assistant was required to hand the task off to Work before any local execution. If the user declined that handoff, local execution was denied entirely.

This is a major behavioral regression because Work/Codex use a separate metered allowance on Plus, with separate 5-hour/weekly limits and optional paid credits / instant resets after the included allowance is exhausted.

Official docs:
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001516-managing-usage-with-gpt-6-astra-in-work-and-codex
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001507-paid-weekly-work-and-codex-rate-limit-resets
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12642688-using-credits-for-flexible-usage-in-chatgpt-personal-plans
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001275-chatgpt-work-and-codex

## Why this is a problem

This is not just a UI preference.

A workflow that was already functioning inside Chat is effectively forced into a separately metered execution experience. The user is asked to move an ongoing project into Work in order to keep doing the same local file/command operations that had already been available in the existing conversation.

For long-running local projects this creates several problems:

1. **Involuntary capability migration**  
   A capability can disappear from an existing conversation without a clear user-facing migration notice.

2. **Separate metering / paid continuation**  
   The replacement execution path consumes the Work/Codex allowance. OpenAI documentation explicitly describes weekly limits, credits, and paid instant resets.

3. **Context continuity risk**  
   Long-running projects may have substantial accumulated context, decisions, state, and verified checkpoints in the original Chat.

4. **User rejection is not the same as capability failure**  
   If the user declines Work because of usage limits, the result is effectively “no local execution,” even though the user has already granted local access to the project through the existing setup.

5. **The product does not clearly distinguish policy/routing from technical capability**  
   The local machine, tools, permissions, and project may all still be available. The blocker is the product routing rule, not the underlying capability.

## Reproduction

1. Use a Plus account with a long-running ChatGPT Project / conversation.
2. Perform a multi-step local workflow in Chat using user-authorized local execution (read/write files, run commands, test changes).
3. Continue the same workflow after the product/session capability update.
4. Ask the assistant to modify/test the same local project.
5. Observe that the assistant is now required to hand off to Work before performing local file or command execution.
6. Decline the Work handoff.
7. Observe that the original Chat can no longer perform the local execution workflow at all.
8. Check Work/Codex usage documentation/settings and observe that the replacement path uses the separate agentic allowance and can offer paid continuation/reset options.

## Expected behavior

Any of the following would be substantially better:

- Preserve already-authorized local execution in existing Chat conversations, **or**
- provide an explicit, user-visible migration notice before removing that capability, **and**
- preserve conversation/project context across the handoff, **and**
- do not force a previously available workflow into a separately metered pool without explicit informed consent.

At minimum, the UI should clearly say:

> “This task used to run in Chat, but local execution is now available only through Work. Work uses a separate allowance and may require credits/reset after limits.”

The user should not discover this only after an assistant suddenly refuses to continue a previously working workflow.

## Related issues

- #43812 — Chat → Work handoff capability exposure issue
- #43931 — Desktop Work local-file execution mode / guidance unclear
- #42215 — Project → local Work handoff / filesystem-stage failures
- #41531 — Work conversation limits break recoverable closeout/handoff
- #50512 — Windows Work approval failure consuming usage without useful output

## Impact

For serious agentic/local-development workflows, this can stop an active project mid-stream and make the user choose between:

- abandoning the existing execution workflow,
- moving to a separately limited Work allowance,
- or paying for additional credits / resets after the included Work allowance is exhausted.

That feels coercive from a user-experience perspective even if it is not intended as such.

The regression is especially frustrating because the local filesystem, permissions, and execution tooling may still exist; the user is being blocked by a routing/product-policy boundary rather than by an unavailable technical capability.

## Privacy

No account identifiers, conversation IDs, repository names, private local paths, credentials, or proprietary project contents are included in this report.

Documentation is missing; documentation is confusing.

## What is the issue?

The ChatGPT Windows desktop Dot profile menu exposes **Rename**, **Pause**, **Reboot**, and **Delete** as separate actions. A screenshot supplied on October 7, 2026 confirms those exact labels. However, the current Dot controls documentation does not explain **Reboot**, and the Help Center getting-started article instead describes a destructive **Reset**.

Please document the supported behavior of the existing **Dot menu → Reboot** control and reconcile the menu terminology across the documentation.

This request concerns the missing user-facing explanation. No Reboot, Reset, or Delete action was performed for this inquiry, and no crash, data loss, or runtime malfunction is being asserted. The exact Windows desktop build and account tier have not been collected; the screenshot establishes the menu labels, not the command's effects.

### Questions the documentation should answer

1. **Scope:** Which components restart or refresh: the Dot coordinator/current agent session, plugin or tool connections, cloud computer/OS, browser, or another component? Does the operation ever replace the cloud environment?
2. **Preserved state:** What survives and what is reloaded or discarded: conversation history versus active working context, saved memories/private notes, cloud files and installed software, browser/login sessions, connected apps, custom rules, and local-computer access?
3. **Active and delegated work:** What happens to an in-flight tool operation and to already delegated local/cloud Codex or Work tasks? Which work stops, remains independent, resumes, or requires explicit continuation?
4. **Recurring work:** Are saved schedules and supported event monitors preserved and enabled? How are runs due during recovery, missed events, and potentially duplicated operations handled?
5. **Automatic lifecycle:** Does OpenAI automatically perform the same operation, can a Dot invoke it itself, and how does it differ from normal pause/wake behavior?
6. **When to use it:** Is Reboot intended for particular recovery symptoms? Is any periodic preventive cadence recommended? Is it required after instructions or plugin changes?
7. **Completion and recovery:** What visible state confirms successful completion, how long should it normally take, and what should users do if it fails? What should users save or check before and afterward?
8. **Terminology:** How do Reboot and Delete in the desktop menu relate to the Help Center's Reset instructions?

### Why it matters

For ongoing Codex coordination and email/calendar checks every 30–60 minutes, users need to know whether this control affects commitments, active tasks, scheduled execution, and stored context. The word “Reboot” alone does not establish those guarantees.

### Related reports and distinct scope

- #49682 includes a controlled Reboot test in which sampled files and the observed kernel boot identifier remained unchanged. Its original missing-file incident and later environment transitions do not establish the command's general behavior.
- #50600 reports a stale plugin tool catalog becoming current after Reboot, explicitly as an observed workaround.
- #50938 reports repeated Reboot attempts that did not restore cloud-computer access; the reporter could not verify completion of the backend operation.

Those reports are related evidence, not an official specification. This documentation request adds the confirmed Windows menu wording, the Reset/Delete terminology mismatch, and the broader questions about delegated work, schedules, automatic lifecycle, and recommended use. - https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots/tasks-and-memory
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001530-getting-started-with-your-dot

items.body:
## Problem

Dot appears to treat **any request involving a local computer** as requiring a separate native Codex/Work task, even when an **already connected and authorized MCP/plugin tool can perform the requested operation directly**.

In my case, I have a plugin that can start and manage agent tasks on my computer. When I ask Dot to use that plugin to delegate work, it instead insists on creating a native Codex task first. That task largely acts as an intermediary, calling or monitoring the plugin rather than doing the work itself.

The issue is **routing**, not missing plugin capabilities, MCP connectivity, or access to existing native Codex threads. Explicitly asking Dot to use the available tool without a native task has not reliably changed the behavior.

## Expected vs. actual

**Expected:**
```
Dot → authorized MCP/plugin tool → requested operation
```

**Actual:**
```
Dot → new native Codex/Work task → authorized MCP/plugin tool → requested operation
```

The distinction is that Dot is **invoking an external API that handles the work**, not itself needing shell access, file access, or computer-use capabilities. The location where the external service executes its work should not automatically force an additional execution task.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Connect a plugin exposing an authorized operation that starts or manages work on a local computer (for example, an agent-thread management integration).
2. Ask Dot to invoke that operation directly.
3. Observe Dot create a native Codex/Work task first, citing the computer-related nature of the request, even though the plugin exposes the necessary action.
4. Repeat while explicitly requesting direct plugin invocation; the extra handoff still occurs.

## Requested behavior

Dot should select an execution route based on **which capabilities the requested operation actually requires**. When an authorized plugin can perform the entire requested action, Dot should be able to call it directly without first creating a native Codex task solely as a wrapper.

If the intermediate task is an intentional product requirement, please clarify that restriction and consider a supported way to select the direct plugin route. Existing permissions and approval safeguards should remain intact.

This introduces unnecessary overhead, splits ownership across multiple task threads, and makes Dot less useful as an orchestrator of external tools.

## Related

#49492 reports a similar forced-handoff symptom when an authorized remote MCP tool could directly perform a file operation. This report focuses specifically on **delegating work through an external tool** instead of creating a redundant native task.

items.body:
## Observed problem

A source-free local browser acceptance test cannot be started through exec_command. The same bounded invocation was rejected twice before process creation with:

```text
exec_command failed: CreateProcess
Rejected(... rejected: blocked by policy)
```

The response does not identify the rule, component or supported remediation. The test has not run; this is not a browser-launch error or a failure at a third-party website.

## Installed environment

- Windows desktop package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1002.7124.0.
- Codex executable resolved on PATH: codex-cli 0.128.0-alpha.1. This is an installed executable observation, not attestation of the rejecting app-server build.
- Active task reports danger-full-access with approval policy never.
- No user rules directory or project-local .codex directory was found at the inspected locations.
- Read-only diagnostic queries recovered the rejection but no named enforcement rule. No security settings were changed.

## Bounded operation

The PowerShell command was intended to create a uniquely named temporary test directory, restrict that new directory to the current user, launch an existing Node/Playwright test against an invented loopback PDF, and remove the empty parent afterward. It does not attach to a personal browser profile, navigate an external source system, use credentials, or read clinical/customer content.

The command combines environment-variable cleanup, Get-ChildItem -Force for an empty-directory check, and non-recursive Remove-Item for the newly allocated parent. No Remove-Item command was passed -Force. The entire invocation was rejected before any of these operations ran. The original command remains private; no raw logs, local paths or session identifiers are included here.

## Static diagnostic candidate, not confirmed cause

In upstream source tagged rust-v0.128.0-alpha.1 (commit 8148b7b1f8660e464661743587f754471ae60868), parse_powershell_invocation uses shlex_split, while has_force_delete_cmdlet checks token segments for a delete cmdlet and a -Force token. Because ordinary newline boundaries may be consumed during tokenization, a -Force option belonging to a directory listing may be associated with a separate Remove-Item command.

Source:
https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8148b7b1f8660e464661743587f754471ae60868/codex-rs/shell-command/src/command_safety/windows_dangerous_commands.rs

This is a static hypothesis, not a confirmed runtime diagnosis. No full-policy side-effect-free evaluator or winning decision was exposed. The source tag has not been attested as the build that rejected the operation.

## Requested resolution

Please identify the blocking component/rule and provide a supported remediation or side-effect-free diagnostic. If the operation is intentionally restricted, please expose an actionable rationale. If command tokenization causes the refusal, please investigate preserving command/parameter ownership when evaluating multiline PowerShell.

We have not changed policy, disabled protection, moved the operation to another executor, or repackaged the rejected action to get around enforcement. We are requesting a supported fix, not a bypass.

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.161.0`; managed daemon `0.161.0`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not relevant to the isolated reproduction: it used a temporary CODEX_HOME without credentials or a model request.

### Which model were you using?

None. This happens during CLI startup, before submitting a prompt.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS, Darwin 25.6.0, arm64. CLI installed through Nix; daemon uses the managed 0.161.0 macOS arm64 package.

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Reproduced through a local PTY.

### Codex doctor report

Relevant checks: CLI 0.161.0, installation consistent, configuration loaded, background app-server running in persistent mode. `codex app-server daemon version` reports both `cliVersion` and `appServerVersion` as `0.161.0`.

### What issue are you seeing?

A persisted daemon feature override survives an explicit restart with the opposite `--enable` flag. The command exits successfully and reports `status: restarted`, but a new CLI session still rejects the daemon.

The daemon settings contain:

```json
{
  "featureOverrides": {
    "api_key_model_discovery": false
  }
}
```

Meanwhile, `codex features list` reports:

```text
api_key_model_discovery  stable  true
```

Running:

```sh
codex app-server daemon restart --enable api_key_model_discovery
```

reports success but leaves the persisted override false. Starting `codex` still shows:

```text
Background server has incompatible feature settings
This session requires api_key_model_discovery to be enabled
```

Selecting the TUI's **Restart with these settings** correctly changes the persisted override to true and fixes startup. I verified a subsequent fresh CLI session reached its normal prompt without the compatibility dialog.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Use CLI and managed daemon 0.161.0 with a saved `featureOverrides.api_key_model_discovery = false` in `$CODEX_HOME/app-server-daemon/settings.json`.
2. Confirm the CLI reports the feature enabled in `codex features list`.
3. Run `codex app-server daemon restart --enable api_key_model_discovery`.
4. Observe successful restart output and exit status 0.
5. Inspect only the relevant boolean in the daemon settings: it remains false.
6. Start `codex`: the incompatible-feature dialog still appears.

I also reproduced the retained override using an isolated temporary CODEX_HOME, the same managed 0.161.0 package, no credentials, and daemon auto-update disabled. In that isolated environment, a separate `daemon stop` followed by `daemon start` removed the saved feature overrides and preserved the other settings. I stopped that test daemon afterward.

### What is the expected behavior?

An explicitly supplied `--enable` or `--disable` on `daemon restart` should apply to the restarted daemon and its persisted launch settings, as the equivalent TUI recovery action does. If lifecycle commands intentionally do not accept feature changes, they should reject the flags or explain that they have no effect rather than reporting an apparently successful repair.

Preserving saved settings for a plain restart with no explicit override makes sense.

### Additional information

This is distinct from #51758 and #51763: matching the CLI and daemon versions did not resolve the persisted override, and the explicit command-line recovery flag was ineffective. The isolated test confirms the behavior does not require active sessions or a version mismatch.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

- Running desktop app: version 26.930.61225, build 13232. Codex is running inside /Applications/ChatGPT.app; its bundle name and executable are ChatGPT.
- Bundled Codex CLI: 0.160.1, a separate version from the desktop app.
- macOS: 27.2, build 26B5091g.
- Architecture: arm64 (Apple silicon); the desktop executable is also arm64.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro 200

### What platform is your computer?

**macOS 27.2 (build 26B5091g), arm64 / Apple silicon.** Verified read-only using OS and architecture queries. Running executable paths were resolved before checking bundle metadata; the bundled executable architecture was also checked.

### What issue are you seeing?

Dot can read delegated tasks on a connected Mac, but parent-to-task continuation can fail even after the user has explicitly approved the intended action in the target session. This is a Dot-to-local-Codex task coordination problem, not a report of model/API network connectivity.

Observed on October 7, 2026:

- `cloud_threads.read` succeeds for the affected task.
- Some `cloud_threads.send_message` continuation attempts return `user cancelled MCP tool call`, with no actual user cancellation observed. The source of cancellation is unknown.
- In another continuation attempt, authorization review rejects approval retrieved from a native human session item as untrusted delegated-tool output. The parent independently reread the item: it was attributed to `role=user`, in a completed turn with `error=null`, and explicitly approved the specific release-installation/resume action. The continuation was still rejected.
- The executor said no further approval was needed, but the parent could not resume it. The user was left needing to send another continuation manually in the executor.

Separately, approximately **17:36–17:48 UTC**, repeated `childEnvironmentDisconnected` notifications arrived across multiple old, completed sessions. During repeated checks, `cloud_threads.list_environments` still reported the same Mac as connected, attached and authorized. Completed tasks remained completed. These observations do not prove that an individual executor transport stayed alive or that the connection inventory itself was wrong.

A separate computer-use task also returned `Transport closed`; a read-only scripting check was interrupted. No message-send command ran in that task. This is additional transport context, not evidence of a common root cause.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed workflow, not yet a deterministic clean-start reproducer:

1. Connect and authorize a Mac for Dot tasks, then create and run a delegated local Codex task.
2. Have the user explicitly approve a narrowly scoped continuation action directly in that target session.
3. From Dot, read the target session and verify the native human approval item and completed turn.
4. Attempt to continue the same task through `cloud_threads.send_message`.
5. Observe a cancellation result or pre-execution approval-attribution rejection instead of a usable continuation.
6. Compare lifecycle notifications with fresh environment inventory and the persisted status of completed tasks.

The cancellation and approval-rejection cases are separate attempts; this report does not claim identical requests produce both errors.

### What is the expected behavior?

- An authorized parent-to-task continuation should reach the intended existing task, or return a precise, actionable reason it cannot.
- Provide a supported, authenticated way to recognize scoped human approval given in the target session. If that approval cannot authorize the parent operation, identify the exact missing approval and show a usable confirmation route.
- Distinguish explicit user cancellation from policy denial, unavailable approval UI, transport failure and other interruptions.
- Make executor lifecycle notifications actionable: correlate them with the affected session and current state, and avoid repeated stale disconnect notices for completed work.

This is not a request to trust arbitrary tool-returned text or bypass authorization/security boundaries.

### Follow-up observation: native tools unavailable in a later turn

At approximately **17:57 UTC on October 7, 2026**, the parent read a new completed turn in the same release task after the user directly sent a continuation in that session.

- Package reverification succeeded, but installation/resume remained paused; neither operation was completed.
- The executor reported that native `read_thread` and `automation_update` were unavailable in its current turn.
- An earlier turn in the same task had `read_thread` available and used it to verify the human authorization.

This latest block is reported missing native-tool availability, not an absence of user consent. The earlier successful `read_thread` use and the later executor report indicate a capability difference across turns. We have not established why the tools became unavailable, nor whether this shares a cause with the continuation, approval-attribution or disconnect symptoms above.

Expected: preserve supported task capabilities across continuations, or explicitly identify a capability change and provide a supported recovery route without repeatedly asking for already-given consent.

### Additional information

**Impact:** work stalls for hours and requires repeated manual continuation/approval handoffs despite successful task reads and a connected-computer inventory.

**Related reports checked:**
- #49729: project-scoped local thread placement/read/message failures. This occurrence differs because the affected task is readable.
- #50168: readable Codex Cloud task with a failing write path. This occurrence uses a connected Mac executor and different errors.
- #50769: later user authorization not reliably recognized in Dot-coordinated workflows. This occurrence adds direct human approval in the target session, an independent reread, and a blocked parent continuation.

Please consolidate or route to the responsible integration team if appropriate. No shared root cause is established, and no app/server implementation diagnosis has been verified.

Prepared with AI assistance at the affected user's request. Private task/account/device identifiers, local paths, project names, release identifiers, and raw conversation contents are omitted.

## Codex sandbox blocks localhost bind during Python regression tests on macOS

### Summary

I am seeing what appears to be a Codex sandbox/runtime issue on macOS where existing Python HTTP tests cannot bind to `127.0.0.1`.

The same Codex session can read/write the workspace and successfully execute hundreds of non-network tests, but local HTTP tests fail specifically when attempting to bind a localhost socket.

This caused Codex to correctly report a repository implementation as NOT READY even though all implementation-specific tests passed.

### Environment

- macOS
- Intel MacBook Pro
- Python 3.12.8
- Codex CLI
- Codex had just performed an automatic update/restart during this work session.
- Project-local Python `.venv`
- Workspace is writable.
- No external network access is required by the failing tests.

Earlier in the same work session I also encountered an unusual Codex startup message:

`Background server has incompatible feature settings`

with:

`This session requires api_key_model_discovery to be disabled`

and options to run without daemon or restart with different shared feature settings.

A subsequent Codex session unexpectedly came up read-only. Restarting/updating Codex fixed the read-only state.

I do not know whether those events are related to the localhost problem, but they occurred during the same session history and may be useful diagnostically.

### Test result

Implementation-specific test suite:

`54 / 54 PASS`

This includes all contract-required fixture/oracle tests.

Full repository regression:

`Ran 689 tests`

Result:

- 683 passed
- 6 errors
- all 6 failures are existing HTTP tests
- failure occurs when the tests attempt to bind localhost / `127.0.0.1`
- no implementation assertion failed

The HTTP/viewer tests were unchanged by the implementation being tested.

### Observed Codex behavior

Codex classified the six failures as sandbox loopback-bind denial.

It attempted to rerun the regression with loopback access, but reported:

`Automatic approval review rejected the full-regression rerun outside the sandbox because this session disables sandbox approvals.`

As a result, Codex could not complete the repository regression gate.

### Important control

The implementation under test does not modify the HTTP/viewer surface exercised by the six failing tests.

The implementation-specific suite passed completely.

The failure class is therefore isolated to tests requiring local socket binding.

### Minimal diagnostic requested

Please check whether the active Codex sandbox allows:

```python
import socket

s = socket.socket()
s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
print(s.getsockname())
s.close()
```

If this returns `PermissionError` / `EPERM` inside Codex but succeeds from the host terminal, the failure appears to be sandbox-policy related rather than repository related.

### Expected behavior

For development/test workloads, Codex should either:

1. permit local loopback bind when the active permission profile authorizes it; or
2. request/obtain the appropriate permission to run localhost-dependent tests; or
3. clearly classify the result as `TEST BLOCKED BY SANDBOX POLICY` rather than making it indistinguishable from a repository regression.

Localhost-only test servers are common for:

- HTTP integration tests
- Playwright/browser tests
- local API tests
- temporary test servers
- websocket tests

They should not require unrestricted external network access.

### Actual behavior

The sandbox appears to prevent the local bind itself.

This leaves the agent unable to satisfy a required full-regression gate even though the tests do not need Internet access.

### Potential related issue

There may also be a permissions/runtime inconsistency around session startup.

During this same workflow:

1. Codex displayed a background-server feature-settings incompatibility involving `api_key_model_discovery`.
2. A subsequent session unexpectedly had read-only filesystem access.
3. Restarting/updating Codex restored workspace writes.
4. The localhost bind restriction remained during the full regression.

I cannot establish causality between these events, but including them may help identify whether different Codex runtime/sandbox profiles were selected across sessions.

### Impact

This can produce false-negative repository audits.

An agent may conclude that an implementation broke regression tests when the actual failure is the Codex execution environment denying localhost binding.

Worse, without a clear environment classification, an agent could attempt to modify otherwise-correct application code or tests to work around a sandbox-only restriction.

### Suggested diagnostic / fix

It would be useful for Codex to distinguish:

`APPLICATION TEST FAILURE`

from:

`SANDBOX CAPABILITY FAILURE`

for operations such as:

- localhost bind
- browser/CDP startup
- local test server startup

A diagnostic message such as:

`6 TESTS NOT EXECUTABLE: LOCAL LOOPBACK BIND DENIED BY ACTIVE SANDBOX`

would prevent the result from being interpreted as an application regression.

If local binding is intended to be configurable, please also verify that the active CLI/background-server permission profile is actually propagated to subprocesses running the test suite.

items.body: On POSIX, a backslash is valid filename text, not a path separator. `PathUri` preserves it in the relative filename, but `TurnDiffTracker::render_diff` currently replaces every backslash in the rendered path with `/`. I confirmed the reproduction with an ordinary tracked file and Git apply; the focused tracker suite passes with the convention-aware fix. This is a path correctness issue; I have no evidence of a security impact.

items.title: Prevent recursive Tokio tracing in telemetry and SQLite logs
items.body:
Prevent recursive Tokio tracing in telemetry and SQLite logs

## Why

Tokio runtime tracing can cause SQLite log writes to enqueue more writes and exporter activity to generate further OTLP exports.

## What changed

- Exclude `tokio` and `runtime` spans from OTLP export alongside `h2` spans.
- Limit `tokio::` and `runtime::` targets to `INFO` in the default log filter, and reject their `TRACE` events directly in the SQLite sink even without an outer filter.
- Box and pin the session-loop future before spawning it.
- Reorder tracing and Tokio test attributes, restrict the skills concurrency test's subscriber to the catalog-refresh span, and use the default log filter in the SQLite formatter comparison test.

items.body:
For identical raw assistant text, the core can emit one plan while streaming and a different plan on completion when a memory citation contains a plan example.

Reproduced against current upstream commit `0e1520605f67969b58e53762be4d675c036a981d`, on Linux with Rust 1.95.0. This is a deterministic core event regression, without an HTTP/model call.

Input:

```text
<proposed_plan>
visible step
</proposed_plan>
<oai-mem-citation>
<proposed_plan>
citation example
</proposed_plan>
</oai-mem-citation>
```

Feed this text through `AssistantMessageStreamParsers` in plan mode, finishing the item, then complete a `ResponseItem::Message` with exactly the same raw text. The ordinary test uses scalar chunks, the real Session event queue, and the completion helper.

Observed events:

- Concatenated `PlanDelta.delta`: `visible step\n`
- `ItemCompleted` containing `TurnItem::Plan.text`: `citation example\n`

Expected: completion should retain `visible step\n`, matching streaming for this unchanged message.

The streaming parser strips citations before plan parsing. `maybe_complete_plan_item_from_message` instead extracts a plan from raw text first and only then strips citations within the selected plan. The two stages do not commute. Moving citation removal before completed-plan extraction resolves this witness and matches the existing streaming order.

A focused fork PR with the two-line fix and ordinary event regression is available at https://github.com/inanna-malick/codex/pull/13.

Reproduction from that PR checkout:

```sh
cd codex-rs
cargo test -p codex-core --lib citation_contained_plan_does_not_replace_the_completed_visible_plan -- --nocapture
```

The new regression failed on unmodified upstream (0 passed / 1 failed) and passed with the fix (1 passed). Related checks passed: 4 turn tests, 3 adapter tests, 15 stream-event tests, 28 upstream stream-parser library tests, core formatting, and diff checks. A separate independent discovery suite also passed 256 cases for each of three properties with both fixed and pre-recorded fresh seeds; the focused PR includes only the ordinary regression and production fix.

```
validate runtime read/execute access on
%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\<runtime>\bin\node_repl.exe:
open ACL target for root-only update:
The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)
setup refresh completed with errors
setup error: setup refresh had errors
```

Stopping node_repl processes did not fully recover execution: the next failure targeted VCRUNTIME140_1.dll loaded by codex-computer-use-swift.exe. Rebooting Windows reproduced the node_repl failure.

## Local controlled measurements
On the active node_repl.exe, CreateFileW was called with share flags 7, OPEN_EXISTING and FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS; handles were immediately closed and no ACLs were changed during the probe:
- READ_CONTROL: success.
- READ_CONTROL | WRITE_DAC: success.
- MAXIMUM_ALLOWED: Windows error 32.

The published rust-v0.162.0-alpha.2 acl.rs uses MAXIMUM_ALLOWED in the root-only ACL update branch with the exact error context. This strongly supports an access-mask sharing conflict, but the installed helper has not been debugger/hash-matched to the source.

## Temporary recovery and validation
With explicit user authorization, original access ACLs were saved and a rollback script preserved. A non-inheriting deny ACE for the current user, limited to FILE_WRITE_DATA | FILE_APPEND_DATA (mask 0x6), was applied to these six bundled runtime files:
- node_repl.exe
- node.exe
- codex-computer-use-swift.exe
- VCRUNTIME140_1.dll
- VCRUNTIME140.dll
- MSVCP140.dll

Afterwards:
- Ordinary sandbox shell commands succeeded under CodexSandboxOffline.
- Project file listing succeeded.
- apply_patch creation, shell reading and apply_patch deletion of a temporary allowed-path probe succeeded.
- Node REPL executed successfully.
- Creating a fresh file outside the allowed workspace was denied.
- Configuration remained elevated.

This is a temporary local workaround, not an upstream fix. It may interfere with in-place runtime updates. No project code was changed.

## Requested fix
Please investigate requesting minimum required access for active EXEs/DLLs when validating ACLs, add regression coverage with bundled runtime processes already running, and provide a supported recovery path. Surface the failing file and Win32 error rather than only helper_unknown_error.

Related reports: #51613, #51601, #51590.

## Duplicate review
Reviewed all five suggested candidates (#51613, #51601, #51634, #51590, #51623). Closing as a duplicate of #51601: the affected core, runtime ACL failure, sharing violation, access-mask-dependent measurements and workaround match the existing reports. #51613 and #51623 have already consolidated their evidence into #51601.

This closure consolidates tracking; it does not indicate an official fix has been released. The independent local measurements and recovery validation remain preserved above.

items.body:
TurnDiffTracker writes filenames directly into Git patch headers. A valid Unix filename containing a tab (for example `a\tb.txt`, where `\t` denotes an actual tab) is consequently decoded as a different filename by Git.

The deterministic regression creates that file with `before\n`, renders its change to `after\n`, and applies the emitted patch to the original temporary directory. Upstream Git application fails with `error: a: No such file or directory`; expected behavior is to update the original filename and preserve its identity.

The fix C-quotes filenames where needed in both the `diff --git` line and the old/new file headers. `/dev/null` handling is preserved. The regression includes plain names, spaces, tabs, quotes and Unicode; filesystem cases with Unix-only filename characters are Unix-scoped.

Validated against upstream `0e1520605f67969b58e53762be4d675c036a981d`, Rust 1.95.0:

- The ordinary regression fails before the fix.
- All 16 focused tracker tests pass after the fix.
- Formatting and diff checks pass.
- The separate discovery property shrank the original failure to one tab. With the repair, 256 generated cases pass at each of seeds `20261007` and independently sampled `7976305664833949441`, with Git as the independent decoder.

Reproduce from `codex-rs`:
```sh
cargo test -p codex-core --lib tracker_diff_preserves_quoted_filenames -- --nocapture
```

The focused branch contains only the production fix and ordinary regression tests. This filename-header mechanism is independent of the previously reported bare-CR content framing issue #51738.

Focused reproduction and fix: https://github.com/inanna-malick/codex/pull/12 (external fork PR).

- ChatGPT für Android aktualisiert

denselben Chatverlauf anzeigen.

This reproduced twice in separate fresh Codex chats and separate starter-project folders. The second run did not reuse the first run's project, recording, or lease. The user's real game project was never opened or imported.

ModRetro support reviewed the report and directed us to OpenAI. OpenAI Help Center support then directed us to this tracker. A `/feedback` report has also been submitted; its private identifier is available to OpenAI Support.

- ChatGPT desktop app: `26.1002.52244`
- Bundled Codex CLI: `0.162.0-alpha.2`

- A `/feedback` report was submitted from the affected Codex chat.
- The affected session transcript and matching desktop logs have been identified and preserved.
- The desktop logs covering the window contain only routine Git-origin entries; the exact close error is present in the Codex transcript.

The private feedback identifier, exact session path, raw transcript, and full configuration can be supplied directly to OpenAI Support. They are omitted from this public issue because they contain account-linked diagnostic metadata, unrelated conversation history, and local paths.

## Configuration summary

- User configuration is at `~/.codex/config.toml`.
- There was no project-local `.codex/config.toml` in the disposable verification workspace.
- There is no custom ModRetro transport, authentication, timeout, command, or environment block.
- The only ModRetro-specific user settings are tool approval rules:

```toml
[plugins."modretro-chromatic@openai-curated-remote".mcp_servers.modretro-chromatic.tools.toolchain_prepare]
approval_mode = "approve"

[plugins."modretro-chromatic@openai-curated-remote".mcp_servers.modretro-chromatic.tools.rom_build]
approval_mode = "approve"
```

## Clean reproduction

1. Started a fresh Codex chat in a new folder.
2. Checked session status and toolchain readiness using the plugin's supported public tools.
3. Created and selected a new disposable starter project.
4. Ran recording-access diagnostics. No prior project lease was reused.
5. Built and inspected the returned ROM successfully.
6. Started a recorded PyBoy boot using project-isolated saves.
7. Advanced to frame 180 and observed genuine 160×144 starter-scene output.
8. Called ordinary `emulator_close` once from the same chat that started the emulator.
9. The close call returned the exact error above.
10. Stopped without retrying, editing/deleting the lease, killing a process, bypassing permissions, changing plugin-cache files, or reinstalling.

## Result after the refused close

- Emulator inactive
- Worker detached
- Worker transports awaiting close: `0`
- Pending requests: `0`
- Lease: `present-unverified`
- Lease capability retained by the local service
- Lease release/normal closure unresolved

The project-local lease path follows this plugin-managed structure:

```text
<disposable-project>/artifacts/.recording-access/lease.json
```

This is plugin-managed project metadata; it is unrelated to GitHub authentication or repository status.

## Expected behavior

The owning chat should be able to close the emulator session it started and release or reconcile the project-local recording-access lease. A final access diagnostic should show no unresolved lease or attached/awaiting-close worker state.

## Requested guidance

1. What supported procedure should reconcile the two retained `present-unverified` test leases without editing or deleting them manually?
2. Is this a known client/plugin lifecycle issue in the listed Codex or ModRetro versions?
3. Is there a fixed version or additional private diagnostic bundle the maintainers need?

Successful build and boot in these disposable projects does not guarantee that normal closure will work in future projects. We will not open the user's real game until the existing lease state has a supported resolution.

### What variant of Codex are you using?

ChatGPT/Codex desktop app with Dots (personal-computer connection).

### What feature would you like to see?

Please add a **Remove/Forget computer** action alongside **Revoke access** in Dots computer management.

#### Use case and observed behavior

I want to manage computers that I no longer want a dot to use, regardless of who owns them. In the interface I used, the available management action appears to be disabling/revoking access; I did not find a separate control to remove a registered computer from the list. Selecting the option to access another computer connects directly, rather than opening a device-management step.

This makes it hard to distinguish a computer that should remain registered with access disabled from one that I want to forget entirely. This is useful when retiring, replacing, or finishing temporary use of a computer, especially when that computer is offline or no longer accessible.

#### Requested behavior

1. Separate registration from authorization in the UI: **Revoke access** disables access while retaining the registered entry; **Remove/Forget computer** removes the registration and the unwanted entry from the computer list.
2. Allow the account owner to revoke access and remove a registered computer from another signed-in device, even when the target computer is offline or unavailable.
3. Removing a computer should also revoke the dot's access. That revocation should take effect even while the computer is offline, so returning online does not restore its previous permission.
4. A removed computer should reconnect only after the user explicitly registers it again **on that computer** and grants access. Returning online or choosing an access-another-computer action should not silently restore the removed registration.
5. Show each registered computer's **last connection time** and **current authorization state**, with online/offline connection status clearly distinguished from access granted/revoked.

This would provide a clear way to retire unwanted devices and reduce accidental reconnection during routine device management.

### Additional information

The [official computer-access documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots/computers-and-apps#connect-your-computer) describes Revoke access and explains that going offline does not revoke the connection. A separate Remove/Forget action would make the registration lifecycle clearer.

Related issues reviewed:

- #49487 reports an unavailable revoke/rebind control when an offline computer must be managed from another device. That overlaps with the offline management requirement here.
- #49824 requests multiple personal computers with independent authorization. This proposal focuses on removing a registration and requiring explicit registration again; it would also be useful under the current single-personal-computer model.

This is a usability and device-lifecycle feature request. If a supported Remove/Forget workflow already exists, guidance on where to find it would also help.

items.body:
## Environment

- Codex CLI: `0.160.0`
- OS: macOS
- Managed daemon enabled

## What happened?

I was working in a long-running Codex CLI session.

The conversation reached automatic context compaction, and the TUI was explicitly showing:

```text
Compacting context...
```

(or `Compacting conversation...`).

While that message was still visible and compaction was in progress, I submitted another prompt.

I expected the new prompt to be queued and processed after compaction completed.

Instead, Codex CLI failed with:

```text
Error: turn/steer failed: Server is draining; retry after reconnecting (code -32600)
```

After restarting Codex CLI, the original session could no longer be resumed normally.

## Recovery behavior after restart

After restarting Codex CLI, it reported that the detected configuration appeared to be intended for an API-key account and offered two options:

1. run without the daemon
2. continue using the detected settings

Choosing the detected settings appeared to do nothing.

Choosing the no-daemon option started Codex, but attempting to resume the original session reported that the session was still being used somewhere else and instructed me to close it there first and then press `R`.

There was no other visible Codex client using the session.

Pressing `R` did nothing.

The only recovery method that worked was **forking the session**. The fork opened successfully and I was able to continue working.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start Codex CLI 0.160.0 on macOS with the managed daemon enabled.
2. Use a session long enough for automatic context compaction to trigger.
3. Wait until the TUI explicitly displays `Compacting context...` / `Compacting conversation...`.
4. While compaction is still running, submit another prompt.
5. Observe:

```text
Error: turn/steer failed: Server is draining; retry after reconnecting (code -32600)
```

6. Restart Codex CLI.
7. Try to resume the original session.
8. The session is reported as still being used by another client.
9. Pressing `R` does not recover it.
10. Forking the session works.

## Expected behavior

Submitting a prompt while context compaction is running should either:

- queue the prompt until compaction finishes, or
- temporarily disable input until the session is ready to accept another turn.

It should not send a `turn/steer` request to an app server that is currently draining.

If the connection is interrupted during compaction, Codex should reconnect and preserve the session state.

After restarting the CLI, stale session ownership from the previous process should be released automatically.

## Actual behavior

Submitting input during context compaction appears to trigger a `turn/steer` request while the server is draining.

This results in:

- `Server is draining` error;
- loss of the active CLI connection;
- original session remaining marked as in use;
- normal resume failing;
- retry (`R`) doing nothing;
- fork being the only working recovery path.

## Possible race condition

This looks like a race between:

1. automatic context compaction starting;
2. the app server entering a draining/reconnect state;
3. the user submitting another prompt;
4. TUI sending that input through `turn/steer`;
5. the old session ownership not being released after the failed connection.

The fact that **fork works while resume does not** suggests that the conversation/thread data itself is probably still valid, while the original session may be left with stale daemon ownership or lifecycle state.

## Additional notes

This may involve an interaction between:

- automatic context compaction;
- `turn/steer`;
- queued user input;
- managed app-server draining/restart;
- stale session ownership after the client disconnects.

Possibly related to existing reports around `Server is draining` and managed daemon/session lifecycle behavior.

- 15:33 onward: task messaging also failed.
- 16:04: fresh-task creation and task listing failed.
- 16:23:39: computer-discovery failure reproduced while recording a performance trace (10:23:39 a.m. America/Edmonton, UTC−06).

### Trace / feedback ID
`no-active-thread-01a1172e-2321-7e81-ae10-4bfda441b8e6`

The identifier is supplied for internal correlation; the trace contents have not been inspected here. The prefix alone is not a root-cause diagnosis.

### Expected behaviour
An authorized, connected computer should remain discoverable, and the existing dot should be able to create and continue permitted tasks. If the conversation-to-dot association becomes invalid, the app should provide a clear recovery path that preserves existing work.

### Impact
Local development and browser-based project monitoring cannot be coordinated despite previously working access. Remaining work is blocked.

### Related reports / additional evidence
The following are other reporters' observations, not independently reproduced on my computer:
- #51742: Windows, the same app version 26.1002.52244; environment discovery and task messaging fail with the exact error while historical task reads work. This appears to be the closest existing match; please consolidate if appropriate.
- #51740: Windows, the same app version; reports task visibility problems plus the active-Aeon error. A comment reports that app/Windows restart and reconnect did not fix it, while manual continuation of an existing task worked: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51740#issuecomment-6042016601 . The visibility symptom may be separate.
- #51730 and #51743: macOS reports with the same error, suggesting it is not confined to Windows or this one desktop version. No maintainer-confirmed shared cause was found during review.
- Matching comments on older issues: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50136#issuecomment-6041779427 ; https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50168#issuecomment-6041841290 ; https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50170#issuecomment-6041728599 . Their original issues concern different problems; the later exact-error comments are the relevant evidence.
- One community commenter reports that right-clicking the dot/name and selecting Reboot helped after app restart/reconnect failed: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51730#issuecomment-6042115683 . Their platform/build is unspecified. I have not tested this workaround or verified its effects.
- #51680, #51735, #51736 and #51732 describe related startup/executor/configuration-service failures. These may help investigation but should not be assumed to have the same cause.

The public status page reported fully operational when checked at 16:12 UTC; that does not rule out this incident or an account-specific fault.

Please correlate the trace with the failing task association and advise a supported recovery. No backend cause is asserted, and private project files, credentials and raw logs are omitted.

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

Root snapshot projection counts repeated persisted copies of the same known assistant source as separate evidence. These duplicates consume the shared 16-message cap and can displace distinct complete user instructions.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The linked regression uses supported APIs to record eight distinct complete user sources and one complete assistant source. It persists eleven copies of that captured assistant envelope, resumes the durable legacy rollout through `ThreadManager`, creates a worker in the resumed tree, and reads the worker's actual root snapshot.

With upstream projection code, only user sources 3 through 7 survive: five user sources rather than the eight distinct sources present in retained history.

Run from `codex-rs` with the regression added:

```sh
cargo test -p codex-core --lib replayed_assistant_source_does_not_displace_distinct_root_instructions -- --nocapture
```

### What is the expected behavior?

A known assistant source should occupy the cap once. The snapshot should contain all eight distinct user sources and one assistant source, with no missing-context markers. Anonymous assistant deliveries should keep their occurrence multiplicity.

### Additional information

Confirmed on upstream `0e1520605f67969b58e53762be4d675c036a981d`, Linux, Rust 1.95.0. The deterministic regression fails before the fix and passes after it. The focused patch retains the original inline projection and admits each known ID once after assistant eligibility checks.

Focused patch and regression: https://github.com/inanna-malick/codex/pull/10

Hi, after deleting an agent/session, I ended up in a state where I could not start new threads normally. Whenever I tried to create a new thread and submit a prompt afterward, the prompt appeared under “Queued follow-up inputs” instead of starting a response. A thread entry was added to the agent center, but trying to open/resume it from there failed with the same error I saw when returning to the deleted agent: ``` Unable to complete action Failed to attach to task: thread/resume failed during TUI bootstrap: thread/resume failed: no rollout found for thread id 01a116cf-6f56-7ca3-8c1d-9981d90ddd6b (code -32600) ``` ### What steps can reproduce the bug? This is the sequence I observed; I have not independently confirmed that it reproduces every time: 1. Have an existing agent/session in the command center. 2. Delete that agent/session. 3. Try creating a new thread and submit a prompt. 4. The prompt stays under “Queued follow-up inputs”, with no response starting, and a thread entry appears in the agent center. 5. Try opening/resuming that thread through the agent center. 6. The TUI fails to attach with the “no rollout found” error above. 7. Further attempts to create threads in that state behaved the same way. Returning to the deleted agent also produced this error. ### What is the expected behavior? Deleting one session should not prevent new threads from starting. A new thread should process its prompt and be resumable from the agent center. Deleted sessions should disappear or clearly say that they are no longer available, rather than leaving me with queued input and an attachment error. ### Additional information The screenshots show the queued prompt and the later resume error. I’m reporting the observed sequence, not claiming that the queueing and resume failure definitely share a root cause.
